messages:
Nora: Quick follow-up to the migration RFC 12: proposing a compatibility manifest service + optional sidecar shim for Private deployments. Wanted to run the idea by runtime/router/ops owners.
Diego: Hmm. How is this different from just using X-RW-Compat headers? Headers are cheap.
Nora: Headers are fine for greenfield, but fragile for long tails (old SDKs, third-party integrators). Manifest is machine-readable, per-tenant+route, and allows richer rules: tombstoned_fields, rename_map, response_wrappers, per-field soft_window_days. Router/runtime cache it and apply transforms.
Mei: Example manifest (conceptual): 
{ route: "/v1/generate", tombstoned_fields: ["meta.trace_id"], rename_map: {"old_field":"legacyField","new_field":"modernField"}, soft_window_days: 21, sidecar_rewrite: true }
Raj: Nice. Distribution: hosted -> router/runtime poll with ETag; Dedicated/Private -> control-plane push or agent sync. Must version manifests (v1, v2) so older runtimes degrade gracefully.
Diego: Behavior question: when a rename is announced, do we emit both fields during soft window or only new one plus a warning header?
Nora: Two-stage: soft window = dual emission (both old and new) + header X-RI-Compat:manifest-v{n}=soft. After signals look good, switch to hard = emit only new_field and mark manifest state as hard. Sidecar will synthesize legacy fields for frozen runtimes.
Mei: Sidecar is useful for on-prem customers who pin runtime versions. But we must cap latency impact. Sidecar will only rewrite response payloads (no CPU heavy work). Provide a low-memory mode and disable for very high QPS routes.
Raj: Telemetry: server-side metric percent_responses_with_legacy_field by tenant+route, client-side sampled warnings (0.1%), and an 'unhandled_field' counter when clients send legacy fields in requests. Correlate with errors/latency by SDK version.
Diego: Migration console idea: show manifest version, % legacy presence, top SDK versions calling legacy, suggested next actions (extend soft window / contact top customers / cut). That helps PMs and CSMs.
Nora: Security: manifest payloads are internal metadata. Pushes to runtimes must be signed by control-plane keys; Private sync requires mTLS agent certs. Never accept unsigned manifests.
Mei: Implementation roadmap (rough): phase 1 (10d) manifest service + router polling + cache; phase 2 (14d) runtime read path + dual-emission logic + telemetry; phase 3 (3w) sidecar binary + packaging + admin UI.
Raj: Backout: if hard cut causes issues, runtime can flip manifest state back to soft per-tenant in minutes, router can inject compat header to force dual-emission, sidecar can be patched. Have an automated rollback toggle in admin console.
Diego: SDK guidance: include a compat helper that fetches manifest (cached 24h) and warns when accessing legacy fields. Example JS snippet: import compat from '@rw/compat' const manifest = await compat.fetchManifest() if (manifest.tombstoned_fields.includes('meta.trace_id')) console.warn('meta.trace_id deprecated')
Mei: Action items: I'll draft manifest schema + sample payloads (due Wed). Diego wire telemetry counters (due Thu). Raj prototype sidecar rewrite rules (POC next sprint). Nora to add RFC addendum.
Nora: One more ask: make soft_window configurable per-field and add a risk_score so faster-safe fields can be removed earlier.
OpsBot: Manifest service deployment scheduled: staging 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z, canary 5% for 48h (pipeline #4789).
